title: Continuously varying exponents in the distribution of waiting times in the symmetric exclusion process on a percolation cluster
authors: Arpan Chatterjee, Kabir Ramola, Deepak Dhar
abstract: We study the waiting-time distribution of hard-core interacting particles in the symmetric exclusion process on one- and two-dimensional lattices with side branches attached to each lattice site in the steady state. We use numerical simulations together with an approximate analytical treatment of particles trapped in side branches in the steady state. Such a two-dimensional carpet serves as a simplified model for trapping of a supercritical percolation cluster. At high particle densities, the system exhibits strong dynamical heterogeneity, with the distribution of logarithms of waiting times developing well-separated peaks corresponding to particles trapped at different depths from the backbone. We show that the probability that a tagged particle occupies the same position at time $t_0+t$ as at time $t_0$ decays algebraically as $t^{-ω}$, where the exponent $ω$ varies continuously with particle density for densities above a threshold value $ρ^*<1$. We also investigate the correlations between successive waiting times along the trajectory of a tagged particle.
summary: This work analyzes particle transport in the Symmetric Exclusion Process on disordered lattices mimicking percolation clusters. It finds that the system's dynamics are characterized by a power-law decay in the return probability, with the decay exponent continuously depending on particle density. This highlights how topological disorder induces strong, density-dependent dynamical heterogeneity.
main_problem: The study investigates the waiting-time distribution of hard-core interacting particles undergoing the Symmetric Exclusion Process (SEP) on complex, disordered geometries like percolation clusters.
main_result: The system exhibits strong dynamical heterogeneity, leading to a power-law decay of the return probability $P_{ret}(t) \sim t^{-\omega}$, where the exponent $\omega$ varies continuously with particle density $ho$.
method: The authors combine numerical simulations with approximate analytical treatments, modeling the system as a backbone with attached side-branch traps.
model_or_system: The model is the SEP on a lattice structure derived from a supercritical percolation cluster, simplified initially by a 'carpet' geometry. The dynamics are governed by hard-core interactions, leading to trapping in side branches.
key_observables: Waiting time distribution ($\psi(	au_w)$), return probability decay exponent ($\omega$), and dynamical heterogeneity peaks in $\log t_w$.
important_parameters: Particle density ($ho$), percolation bond probability ($p$), and the correlation length ($\xi$) related to the cluster structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on approximating the complex cluster dynamics by considering contributions from individual side branches (single-branch approximation), though multi-branch models improve accuracy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate representative spanning clusters, schematic diagrams of the carpet/comb model, and plots showing the power-law decay of survival probabilities and waiting time histograms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from studying the SEP on simplified geometries (carpet) to developing analytical tools based on eigenvalue expansions for single branches, culminating in the application to full, irregular percolation clusters to derive the density-dependent exponent $\omega$.
why_interesting: The connection between topological disorder (percolation) and non-equilibrium dynamics (SEP) is highly relevant to understanding transport in disordered quantum systems, such as those modeled by disordered spin glasses or quantum impurities.

The left panel shows a critical bond percolation cluster generated on a 200 × 200 lattice, with the backbone highlighted in blue and side branches highlighted in green. For clarity, only a subset of the possible particle hopping moves is shown. Bottom: The carpet graph with side branches of depth H = 2.

Con- sider first the red–green pair: at time t, the red particle is selected for an LSEP move in direction +ˆy with displacement D = 8. The red particle immediately collides with the green particle, which then propagates freely for three steps before colliding with the pink particle. The pink particle continues for the remaining three steps, wrapping once around the peri- odic lattice to complete the move. Particles enter and leave the branch through the rightmost site, which is connected to a particle reservoir maintained at density ρ. Entry and exit occur with rates p = ρ and q = 1 −ρ, respectively. The transitions indi- cated by dotted arrows occur with unit rate.
